title: Being a local complete intersection over a field is invariant under extension of the field
statement: Let $k$ and $K$ be fields, $\iota:k\to K$ a ring homomorphism (making $K$ a $k$-algebra), and $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then $S\otimes_kK$, a $K$-algebra through $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$, is a finite type $K$-algebra, and $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] if and only if $S\otimes_kK$ is a local complete intersection over $K$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SJ (label lemma-lci-field-change, line 36262); proof lines 36269-36330 (via Lemma 00SC lemma-lci and flatness of k[x]_{p'} -> K[x]_{q'}; or Lemmas lemma-lci-global and lemma-lci-field-change-local)

proof.text: Choose a surjection $\alpha:P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow S$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-conormal-field-comparison]: with $I=\ker\alpha$, $P_K=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $I_K=\rho(I)P_K$, identify $S=P/I$ through $\alpha$; then $S_K=S\otimes_kK\cong P_K/I_K$, finite type over $K$, $M=I/I^2$ finite over $S$, and $M_K=I_K/I_K^2\cong M\otimes_SS_K$ as $S_K$-modules.

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), proof, using the conormal-generator route of Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local) and Tag 00SC (lemma-lci).

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S_K$ contracting to $\mathfrak p\subset S$, [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localized-module-base-change] gives $M_{K,\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}S_{K,\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension], $d=\dim_{\mathfrak p}\operatorname{Spec}S=\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Spec}S_K$. The conormal residue fibres are related by extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ to $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, with equal finite dimensions, by [lem-trf-lci-conormal-fibre-field-change] under $\tau:S\otimes_kK\to K\otimes_kS$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes s$. Use the prime $\widetilde{\mathfrak q}=\tau(\mathfrak q)$ in $K\otimes_kS$ and presentation $\tau\alpha_K$: its kernel remains $I_K$ and $\tau\alpha_K(x_i)=1\otimes\alpha(x_i)$. Since $\tau(j(s))=1\otimes s$, contraction is still $\mathfrak p$ and the residue-field maps agree.

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), proof, using the conormal-generator route of Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local) and Tag 00SC (lemma-lci).

proof.text: Assume $S$ is LCI. At each $\mathfrak q$, choose a principal global-CI neighbourhood of its contraction $\mathfrak p$ using [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension], $0\leq d\leq n$ and $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is free of rank $n-d$. Step 2 carries its basis to $n-d$ generators upstairs: expand every first tensor factor in that basis. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-generators-global-complete-intersection] there is $h\notin\mathfrak q$ with $(S_K)_h$ global CI. These $D(h)$ cover because each contains its chosen prime; hence $S_K$ is LCI by the definition.

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), proof, using the conormal-generator route of Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local) and Tag 00SC (lemma-lci).

proof.text: Conversely assume $S_K$ is LCI. The map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective (both spectra consist of $(0)$), so [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change] supplies a prime $\mathfrak q$ above each $\mathfrak p\subset S$. At $\mathfrak q$, the definition and [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] give a free conormal module of rank $n-d$. Its residue fibre has dimension $n-d$. Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-residue-extension-minimal-generators], applied to $M_{\mathfrak p}$ (finite: localize the generators from step 1), give $n-d$ generators downstairs, including when $n-d=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-generators-global-complete-intersection] there is $g\notin\mathfrak p$ with $S_g$ global CI. These principal opens cover, so $S$ is LCI by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].
